1.say: Cut off one clear RJ45 plug from one end of your blue network cable. Keep the other original plug on, leaving one flat-cut bare jacket end.
placements: clear plastic RJ45 plug on blue patch cable → cut off and removed, leaving flat-cut bare blue jacket end on coiled cable (in the video: cable coiled on dark table with one plug left on; cutting tool not named, match the picture)
watch_for: If both ends are bare you cut too much — you need one original clear plug still on the cable to keep the 568B end
If the blue jacket end is angled or frayed, recut it flat — the stripper needs a clean start
1.check_yourself: The blue cable lies coiled with one clear plug still attached and one flat-cut bare jacket end.
1.safety: Keep your fingers well away from the cutter blade and cut away from your body.

2.say: Push the flat-cut bare end of the blue cable into your wire strippers. Strip off about an inch of blue outer jacket to expose the eight small colored inner wires.
placements: blue outer jacket at flat-cut bare end of blue cable → stripped back about 1 inch with wire strippers (in the video: yellow-handled strippers around blue jacket on dark table), exposing eight small colored wires sticking out of blue jacket
watch_for: If the small colored wires look nicked or copper shows, you squeezed too hard — the jacket should pull off clean without cutting inner insulation
If less than about an inch shows you stripped too little — you need enough length to untwist and line up
2.check_yourself: The cut end shows eight small colored wires sticking out about an inch from the blue jacket.
2.safety: Keep fingers clear of the stripper blades and pull the jacket away from your hand.

3.say: Snip the white string filler flush at the blue jacket edge and throw it away. Untwist and finger-straighten all eight small colored wires so they fan straight out with no twists.
placements: white string filler among inner wires at blue jacket edge → snipped off flush at jacket and discarded (in the video: cut with cutter jaws on dark table)
eight twisted small colored wires sticking out of blue jacket → separated, untwisted and straightened to eight straight wires fanning out from blue jacket with no twists
watch_for: If wires still curl or stick together, they are still twisted — if the plug mis-wires, straighten again until flat
If the white string is still sticking out among the wires, you forgot to cut it — it will block the plug if left in
3.check_yourself: Eight straight inner wires fan out from the blue jacket with no twists and no white string.
3.safety: Keep fingertips away from the cutter blade when you snip the white string.

4.say: Pick up the small blue rubber boot. Slide it over the exposed wire tips down onto the blue cable to sit below the exposed wires.
placements: small blue rubber strain-relief boot → slid over exposed wire tips down onto blue outer jacket to sit loose around blue cable below exposed wires (in the video: on dark table; taper direction not readable, match the picture)
watch_for: If you forget the boot now you cannot add it after crimping — if the plug is already crimped without the boot you must cut off and restart
If the boot slides off the cable end, push it far enough down the blue jacket that the wires stay exposed above it
4.check_yourself: A small blue boot sits loose around the blue cable below the exposed wires.

5.say: Fan the eight straight colored wires flat side-by-side in 568A order white-green, green, white-orange, blue, white-blue, orange, white-brown, brown. Trim the tips straight across even for insertion.
placements: eight straight colored wires at blue jacket with blue boot below → arranged flat parallel left-to-right in TIA 568A order: 1 white-green, 2 green, 3 white-orange, 4 blue, 5 white-blue, 6 orange, 7 white-brown, 8 brown (in the video: pinched between fingers on dark table, green-first on left, orange-handled crimp tool behind)
uneven tips of ordered wires → trimmed straight across even with cutter to short even length ready to insert (the video doesn't state trim length; match the picture)
watch_for: If orange comes first instead of green you lined up 568B by mistake — green pair must be first for this 568A end
If tips are staggered or splayed the plug will miss a wire — if colors don't reach the front together, re-flatten and trim again
5.check_yourself: Eight flat parallel wires extend in green-first 568A order with even-cut tips ready to insert.
5.safety: Keep fingers out of the cutter blades when you trim the wire tips even.

6.say: Pick up a new clear rectangular RJ45 plug. Push the eight ordered flat wires fully into its back until each colored tip shows at the front.
placements: eight ordered flat wires with blue jacket and loose blue boot below → pushed into rear opening of new clear RJ45 plug until colored wire ends are visible reaching the front under gold pins (in the video: plug pinched in fingers on dark table, boot left down on jacket)
watch_for: If the color order flips or crosses while pushing, you twisted the bundle — if the front view is out of order, pull out and re-line up
If wire tips stop short of the front, you didn't push far enough — the colors must be visible at the clear front end
6.check_yourself: The clear plug sits on the wire ends with all colored wires visible reaching the front.

7.say: Set the wired clear plug into the RJ45 socket of your crimping tool. Squeeze the handles firmly to crimp the plug onto the wires and jacket.
placements: wired clear RJ45 plug with blue jacket at its rear and blue boot below → inserted into RJ45 crimp socket at front of black-and-orange crimping tool on dark table and squeezed, leaving clear plug flattened onto wires with blue jacket tucked inside plug rear
watch_for: If the plug still wiggles on the wires you under-crimped — the gold pins must be driven down and the plug tight
If the blue jacket hangs outside the plug rear you missed strain relief — the jacket must be tucked inside the plug before crimping
7.check_yourself: The clear plug is tightly flattened onto the wires with blue jacket tucked inside the plug rear.
7.safety: Keep your fingers out of the crimp jaws and handle pivot when you squeeze — it pinches hard.

8.say: Grip the small blue boot on the blue cable. Slide it forward up over the back of the crimped clear plug until it covers the joint.
placements: small blue boot around blue cable below crimped plug → slid forward up over rear of clear plug to cover the back of the plug where blue jacket enters (in the video: finished crossover end held in fingers on dark table)
watch_for: If the boot sits crooked or leaves a gap at the plug back, you stopped short — push it fully forward until it hugs the plug
If the boot pushes the plug sideways, you forced it — wiggle straight on, don't bend the crimped wires
8.check_yourself: The blue boot covers the back of the clear plug on the finished crossover end.
